body:
## Summary
- `hello` upstream version check silently no-op'd on fresh personal-repo clones: only `origin` is configured, so `git fetch upstream` failed and the gate never fired.
- Every fresh env (mobile sandbox resets each session, new desktops) ran stale framework undetected — defeats the core "never miss a framework update for more than a week" design intent.
- Fix: `hello` now verifies `upstream` exists and auto-adds it (`git remote add upstream https://github.com/cordfuse/cortex.git`) before the fetch. URL is already a trusted remote via guardrails — no new trust surface.

## Surfaced by
v3.3.1 mobile test checklist check #1 (FAIL). Root cause filed in `steve-krisjanovs/cortex` `records/2026-04-23-2107-bug-upstream-gate-missing-remote.md`. Fix option B from that record (protocol-level auto-repair) — recommended as self-healing and covers mobile + desktop + any clone method.

## Changes
- `protocol/CORTEX.md` — Opening (`hello`) upstream version check prepended with the existence check + auto-add.
- `version.txt` → 3.3.2
- `cortex-changelog.md` — two new entries at top.

## Test plan
- [ ] Fresh clone of `steve-krisjanovs/cortex` into a sandbox with no `upstream` remote.
- [ ] Run `hello`.
- [ ] Verify scribe auto-adds `upstream` without prompting, fetches, and fires the gate prompt if versions differ.
- [ ] Verify re-running `hello` on a clone that already has `upstream` does not duplicate the remote (`git remote add` no-ops or errors safely — confirm scribe handles).

## Related
- Companion bug still open: sync scope bootstrap — `records/2026-04-23-2110-bug-sync-scope-bootstrap.md`. Separate PR.

author: chrisbodhi
body:
## Summary

Introduces automated verification that the Platerator API documentation and Claude skill stay in sync with the OpenAPI-relevant source code, plus per-edit fast checks for Rust and TypeScript. These checks run both in the Claude editor (via `PostToolUse` hooks) and in CI.

## Key Changes

- **`scripts/check-api-sync.sh`** — Single source of truth for verifying API docs consistency. Hashes OpenAPI-relevant source files (`crates/web/src/lib.rs`, `crates/domain/src/lib.rs`) and compares against a committed hash. Runs from both the Claude `PostToolUse` hook and CI, emitting GitHub Actions annotations and step summary blocks on mismatch.

- **`scripts/post-edit-checks.sh`** — Non-blocking per-edit checks dispatched by file path:
  - Rust files → `cargo clippy -p <crate> -- -D warnings`
  - TypeScript files → `bun run typecheck`
  - Failures print to stderr and emit `::warning::` annotations in CI, but never roll back edits.

- **`.claude/settings.json`** — New Claude configuration file that wires both check scripts to the `PostToolUse` hook, firing after every `Edit`/`Write`/`MultiEdit`.

- **`.claude/skills/platerator-api/SKILL.md`** — New comprehensive skill documentation covering:
  - All REST endpoints (validate, generate, download)
  - Request/response schemas with field reference tables
  - End-to-end example (validate → generate → download)
  - Common error cases and remediation

- **`.claude/skills/platerator-api/.api-hash`** — Committed hash file tracking the current state of OpenAPI-relevant source.

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — Updated to document the sync verification workflow, per-edit checks, and remediation steps. Added `expected_force_per_pin` field to the API example.

- **`justfile`** — Added `check-api-sync` and `update-api-hash` targets for manual verification and hash refresh.

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — Added `check-api-sync.sh` to the `test-rust` job so API drift is caught on every PR.

## Implementation Details

- The hash is computed by SHA256-hashing each input file, then SHA256-hashing the concatenated list, making reordering or renaming detectable.
- When a mismatch is detected, the script emits:
  - A GitHub Actions file-level `::error::` annotation (visible on PR Files tab)
  - A markdown block in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (visible in `gh run view` and run summary page)
  - Plain remediation text on stderr (for Claude hooks and local terminals)
- Per-edit checks always exit 0 so failures never block the edit; they're purely informational.
- The skill and docs are now the source of truth for API consumers; the hash ensures they stay current with implementation changes.

## Summary by cubic
Moves GitHub runtime detection to server-side `VM_START` to eliminate races and reliably provision VMs with the correct package manager and dev port. Also hardens advisory lock handling and simplifies VM resume logic, while removing client-side runtime probing.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Fixed a race where `VM_START` could start before the client wrote `runtime`, creating clone-only daemons. Server-side lockfile probe now runs inside `VM_START` and persists the result.
  - Bounded advisory lock waits in `KyselySandboxRunnerStateStore` with `statement_timeout` and clearer errors to avoid wedging on slow holders.

- **Refactors**
  - Added `github-runtime-detect` for server-side lockfile probing and optional port extraction; `VM_START` uses it when metadata lacks a package manager and writes back to metadata (`runtime: { selected, port }`).
  - Simplified `FreestyleSandboxRunner.ensure` and made VM resume failures silent (returns null) to trigger recreate.
  - Trimmed `github-repo-picker.tsx` to only fetch `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`; removed client runtime detection.
  - Switched `useChatStream` to `useChatBridge` in the visual editor prompt.
  - Updated agent shell auto-start to dedupe per-branch attempts and avoid resurrecting a VM after user delete.

author: twaldin
body:
## What's new

This release lands the four frontier adapters (`crush`, `factory-droid`,
`kilo`, `openclaude`) added in the prior batch, plus the in-flight
container-bringup fixes that came out of real-world benchmarking. After
this PR, those adapters reliably build commands and resolve models in
both bare host and Linux container environments.

### highlights

- **factory-droid BYOK works.** Drop `--auto`, keep
  `--skip-permissions-unsafe`, auto-prefix `custom:` onto bare model ids
  so the BYOK flow against the user's own OpenAI-compatible endpoint
  goes through.
- **openclaude env-mode for OpenAI-compat endpoints.** When
  `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` is set, switch to
  `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_OPENAI=1` + `OPENAI_MODEL=...` and drop `--model`,
  matching openclaude's documented usage.
- **continue-cli OpenAI-compat config.** With OpenAI env present, write
  a minimal Continue config YAML in workdir and call
  `cn -p --config <path> --format json` so bare ids like `gpt-5.4` work
  end-to-end.
- **kilo container path tolerance.** Wrap host-side parent `mkdir` in
  try/except so a `KILO_DB` pointing at `/app/...` no longer aborts the
  command build on the host.
- **crush.** Argv reordered to `run --data-dir <dir> --model ...`;
  preserve explicit `provider/model` when caller is being explicit.
- **`--model-no-resolve` escape hatch.** New CLI flag and
  `RunSpec.model_no_resolve` / `modelNoResolve` field — pass the model
  string through verbatim for odd provider/model combos that the
  best-effort resolver doesn't know about.
- **Model normalization additions.** `KNOWN_PROVIDERS` learns
  `openai-codex` and `azure-openai-responses`. `pi` resolves bare
  `gpt-5.x` to `openai-codex/gpt-5.x`. `crush` joins
  `PRESERVE_EXPLICIT_PROVIDER_HARNESSES`.

### adapters touched (py + ts)

`aider`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `continue-cli`, `crush`,
`factory-droid`, `gemini`, `kilo`, `openclaude`, `opencode`, `pi`,
`qwen`, `swe-agent` -- every adapter now threads the
`model_no_resolve` / `modelNoResolve` flag through to
`normalize_model_for_harness` / `normalizeModelForHarness`.

The five behavioral changes (factory-droid, openclaude, continue-cli,
kilo, crush) are also mirrored on the TS side.

### docs / scaffolding

- `.nvmrc` pinned to Node `20.20.2` for host dev.
- `scripts/check_binaries.sh` -- "is this harness installed" check for
  the gpt-5.4 set.
- `scripts/smoke_gpt54.py` -- minimal "ask harness X to write hi.txt"
  smoke runner. Useful for bringup, not part of the core library.
- `README.md` documents `--model-no-resolve` and adds a "model
  resolution policy" section that frames resolution as deliberately
  best-effort.
- `SPEC.md` documents the new optional `modelNoResolve` field.

## Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q`: **91/91 passing** (includes new
  `test_model_normalization.py` cases for pi gpt-5 routing,
  `--model-no-resolve` raw passthrough, factory-droid `custom:`
  auto-prefix, and double-prefix protection on the new providers; plus
  new CLI tests that the `--model-no-resolve` flag survives the typer
  layer into the `RunSpec`).
- `bun test` in `ts/`: **42/42 passing** (37 pre-existing + 5 new
  normalization tests mirroring the py additions).
- Real-world: a 712-run TB2 benchmark sweep is currently in flight in
  `~/harness-bench` running against this exact code (PYTHONPATH points
  at `~/harness/src`). The factory-droid, openclaude, kilo, and
  continue-cli adjustments here all came directly out of failures
  observed in that sweep.

## Versions

- `harness-cli` (PyPI): `0.2.2` -> `0.3.0`
- `@twaldin/harness-ts` (npm): `0.1.2` -> `0.2.0`

Tag and publish workflows fire on `py-v*.*.*` / `ts-v*.*.*` push -- not
tagging in this PR, that step is left for the manual merge.

author: nash87
body:
## Summary
Mirrors the parkhub-rust PR #373 fix for two Codex-flagged silent-fail bugs already shipped on main via #331.

- **Calendar query mismatch**: `api.calendarEvents(start, end)` serialized to `?start=...&end=...`, but `BookingCalendarController::calendarEvents` reads `from`/`to`. The month-scope filter was silently dropped → unbounded event set + stale Kalender counts + payload bloat. Rename positional params and build the query via `URLSearchParams`.
- **Buchen invalid-datetime silent fail**: `new Date(startDate).toISOString()` throws `RangeError` on an empty `datetime-local`. The exception fires inside the onClick, the mutation never fires, and the user sees nothing happen. Added an `isValidDt` guard that surfaces a German error toast.

## Test plan

author: ryan-reese
body: # ALCHEMI Toolkit Pull Request ## Description `EwaldModelWrapper` and `PMEModelWrapper` keeps a persistent `self._energies_buf` tensor and reuses it each forward via `zero_()` + `scatter_add_(0, batch_idx, per_atom_energies)`. Because `per_atom_energies` carries a `grad_fn` from the Warp backward tape, the in-place ops chain each step's autograd graph onto the buffer through PyTorch's version-counter mechanism. The buffer is owned by `self`, so the chain cannot be GC'd — per-step cost grows linearly and GPU memory climbs unboundedly in long MD runs. This PR calls `detach_()` after the clone to break the autograd chain. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] Performance improvement - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes) - [ ] CI/CD or infrastructure change ## Related Issues N/A — bug surfaced during downstream MD integration work, not tracked in an existing issue. ## Changes Made - `nvalchemi/models/ewald.py`, `nvalchemi/models/pme.py`: for `self._energies_buf`, zero buffer per `forward()`, scatter into it, call `detach_()` after the clone, so callers continue to receive a tensor with independent storage (matches the prior output contract; some downstream consumers mutate `batch.energy` in place). - `test/models/test_ewald.py`, `test/models/test_pme.py`: add two regression tests per wrapper — one checks `_energies_buf.grad_fn is None`, one asserts consecutive forwards return energy tensors whose storage is independent of prior outputs. - `CHANGELOG.md`: add entry under Unreleased. ## Testing - [x] Unit tests pass locally - [x] Linting passes (`make lint`) - [x] New tests added for new functionality meets coverage expectations? ### Empirical verification 1000 NVT Langevin steps, naphthalene (3,6,3) = 1944 atoms, PBC, AIMNet2 + electrostatics (`accuracy=1e-6`, `hybrid_forces=False`, `compile_model=True`), dt = 1.5 fs, T = 200 K, friction = 0.01, 50-step timing blocks. Tested on: NVIDIA H100 NVL (95 GB, driver 570.195.03), ARM (Linux 6.8.0), PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), Python 3.12.13. | | step 50 ms/step | step 950 ms/step | last / first | GPU mem start | GPU mem end | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Ewald (unfixed) | 146.5 | 456.9 | 3.1× | 175.8 MB | 196.5 MB | | Ewald (fixed) | 94.4 | 79.7 | 0.84 (warmup) | 174.7 MB | 174.7 MB | | PME (unfixed) | 111.8 | 568.6 | 5.1× | 183.9 MB | 204.6 MB | | PME (fixed) | 91.6 | 76.0 | 0.83 (warmup) | 182.8 MB | 182.8 MB | Figure (per-step runtime + GPU memory vs step, all four configs) attached below. **Numerical equivalence.** GPU `scatter_add_` is non-deterministic (atomic-add ordering), so neither variant is bit-exact against itself. Measured relative L2 deltas of per-atom positions and forces at step 20 (seed = 42): unfixed-vs-fixed deltas are within same-code run-to-run envelope for both models. No systematic shift. ## Checklist - [x] I have read and understand the [Contributing Guidelines](../CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I have updated the [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) - [x] I have performed a self-review of my code - [x] I have added docstrings to new functions/classes - [ ] I have updated the documentation (if applicable) ## Additional Notes `nvalchemi/models/lj.py` has a superficially similar pattern but with `self._atomic_energies_buf` (a kernel output buffer) on the scatter.

## Summary

Eight new read-only tools for network-layer correlation and site-outage detection. Closes the gap that let a customer power outage escape correlation — adds the primitives and composites that catch the class of site-outage signature (collector down + mass interface-down + UPS on-battery + downstream device silence) that generic AIOps correlation misses.

## Tools added (8)

**Primitives (5, in new `src/lm_mcp/tools/networking.py`):**
- `get_interface_metrics` — per-interface time-series (bytes, errors, discards, utilization, status)
- `get_top_talkers` — NetFlow ranking by src/dst/protocol/application/pair
- `detect_alert_burst` — sliding-window mass-event detector
- `get_link_flaps` — interfaces with repeated up/down transitions
- `get_power_events` — UPS/PDU alert filter across APC/Liebert/Eaton

**Collector enrichment (1, appended to `collectors.py`):**
- `get_collector_health` — time-since-last-contact, downstream device count, CollectorDown history

**Composite workflows (2, appended to `workflows.py`):**
- `detect_site_outage` — chains CollectorDown + interface burst + UPS events + device silence into confidence-scored verdict
- `audit_network_monitoring_coverage` — portal coverage audit with prioritized gap list

243 -> 251 LM tools. Overall (LM + AAP + Terraform + watsonx): 272 -> 280.

author: jlinoff
body:
The CSS URL was built using window.location.origin + '/css/print-report.css', which gives the correct path on localhost but fails on GitHub Pages and other sub-path deployments where the app is served from a path below the origin (e.g. https://jlinoff.github.io/pam/www/).  In that case the CSS 404s silently and the print report renders completely unstyled.

Fix: derive the CSS URL relative to the page base instead:
  1. Use <base href> if present
  2. Otherwise strip the filename from window.location.href to get the directory (e.g. https://jlinoff.github.io/pam/www/)
  3. Resolve via new URL('css/print-report.css', base)

This is correct for localhost, GitHub Pages, and any other sub-path deployment without hardcoding paths.

No test changes — localhost tests are unaffected since origin and base path are identical there.

Files changed:
  www/js/print.js
  VERSION

author: venksrin09
body:
## Summary
Fixes #37 and #38 - Two UX issues affecting session usability.

## Issue #37: Remove misleading srun/sbatch examples
**Problem**: The frontend displayed examples using `srun` and `sbatch` commands, but these Slurm CLI tools are not installed in session containers. Users were misled by the UI showing commands that don't work.

**Solution**: Replaced with accurate, generic examples showing:
- Checking allocated GPUs via environment variables (`$SPUR_JOB_GPUS`, `$ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES`)
- Installing packages as needed (`pip install`)
- Running user workloads (user decides what to run in the bash shell)

## Issue #38: Fix rocm-smi inconsistent availability  
**Problem**: The `rocm-smi` command was configured as a bash alias in `/etc/profile.d/spur-gpu.sh`, which only works in login shells. This caused intermittent failures in:
- Web terminal (uses `bash` not `bash -l`)
- Direct SSH command execution (`ssh host 'rocm-smi'`)
- Non-interactive shells

**Solution**: Replaced bash alias with an executable wrapper script at `/usr/local/bin/rocm-smi` that:
- Intercepts all rocm-smi calls
- Automatically adds `-d $SPUR_JOB_GPUS` flag to filter to allocated GPUs
- Works in all shell contexts (login, non-login, interactive, non-interactive)

## Changes
- `frontend/src/pages/SessionDetail.tsx`: Removed srun/sbatch examples, added generic session usage examples
- `crates/spur-cloud-api/src/spur_client.rs`: Created rocm-smi wrapper script instead of alias

## Testing
- ✅ Rust backend: `cargo check` passes with no errors
- ✅ Frontend: `npm run build` completes successfully  
- ✅ Wrapper script: bash syntax validated
- ✅ Both K8s and bare-metal deployment modes supported

## Verification Steps
1. Launch a session with SSH enabled
2. Open web terminal → run `rocm-smi` → should work
3. SSH to session → run `rocm-smi` directly → should work
4. Run `ssh session 'rocm-smi'` (non-login shell) → should work
5. Verify UI shows correct examples (no srun/sbatch references)

## Backward Compatibility
- No breaking changes
- Frontend-only changes for Issue #37
- Existing sessions continue to use alias (login shells only)
- New sessions get wrapper script (works everywhere)

author: adamwoodnz
body:
Fixes [RSM-1071](https://linear.app/a8c/issue/RSM-1071/search-30-compact-search-pattern-with-inline-filter-sort-controls)

<!-- Linear: https://linear.app/a8c/issue/RSM-1071/search-30-compact-search-pattern-with-inline-filter-sort-controls -->

## Proposed changes

Adds a **Compact Search** Jetpack Search block pattern: a single-row toolbar (search + filter popover + sort popover) over a dense result list, inspired by the WordPress Dataview list layout.

- **New block**: `jetpack/filter-popover` — a container for `filter-checkbox` + `active-filters` inner blocks, surfaced as an icon trigger with an active-filter count badge; opens a `role="dialog"` panel.
- **Existing blocks extended**:
  - `jetpack/search-results` now supports `layout: "card" | "compact"`. Compact mode hides the breadcrumb path and image, renders title + date in a dense row, and omits author bylines to match normal single-site Instant Search result metadata.
  - `jetpack/sort-control` now supports `displayAs: "select" | "radio" | "popover"`. Popover mode renders an icon trigger -> `role="menu"` with `menuitemradio` options, and still supports older saved `display="popover"` block markup.
- **Interactivity store**: adds `isFilterPopoverOpen` / `isSortPopoverOpen` state, `toggleFilterPopover` / `toggleSortPopover` / `closeAllPopovers` / `selectSortOrder` actions, `onWindowClickClosePopovers` / `onEscapeClosePopovers` window handlers for Dataview-style outside-click + Esc close, plus `activeFilterCount` and sort-state derived getters.
- **Editor previews**: compact preview states now mirror the front-end default/successful-results state: popovers are closed by default, and the no-results message is not shown alongside sample results.
- **Result data**: result card normalization keeps only fields the Search block UI renders; author byline data is not exposed for compact results.
- **Pattern**: new `compact-search.php` composes `search-input` + `filter-popover` (with category / tag / post-type `filter-checkbox` children) + `sort-control[displayAs=popover]` + `results-count` + `search-results[layout=compact]` + `no-results` + `load-more`.

All new styles use `currentColor` / `color-mix` / `var(--wp--preset--color--background)` so they inherit the active theme palette.

## Related product discussion/links

- Linear: [RSM-1071](https://linear.app/a8c/issue/RSM-1071/search-30-compact-search-pattern-with-inline-filter-sort-controls)

## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use?

No.

## Testing instructions

Requires the Jetpack Search blocks feature flag to be enabled.

If Jetpack Instant Search is enabled on the test site, disable it before testing on a search results page; otherwise the Instant Search overlay intercepts `?s=...` requests and the compact toolbar cannot be exercised.

1. In a wp-env (or any WP site with this package mounted), create a new page.
2. Open the block inserter -> **Patterns** -> **Jetpack Search** -> insert **Compact Search**.
3. Save and view the page.

**Editor preview:**

- The inserted pattern preview shows the compact toolbar and sample results.
- The filter and sort popovers are closed by default.
- The no-results message is not displayed under the sample results.
- Compact sample results show title + date only; no author byline is displayed.

**Golden path:**

- You see a single row containing: a search input on the left, and a **filter** icon + **sort** icon on the right.
- Results render below as a compact list: title + date, no author, no excerpt/image, tight vertical rhythm.

**Filter popover:**

- Click the filter icon. A popover opens containing the **Active Filters** summary plus **Category**, **Tag**, and **Post Type** checkbox lists (each with live aggregation counts).
- Tick one or more checkboxes — results update, the popover stays open, and a numeric **badge** appears on the filter trigger showing the total count of selected values across all dimensions.
- Close the popover. Re-open. State is preserved.

**Sort popover:**

- Click the sort icon. A menu opens with **Relevance**, **Newest**, **Oldest**. The currently selected option shows a checkmark.
- Pick a different option — the list resorts and the popover closes.

**Accessibility / Dataview parity:**

- Tab order reaches search input -> filter trigger -> sort trigger.
- Open a popover: the trigger's `aria-expanded` flips to `true`.
- Press `Escape` — the open popover closes.
- Click outside an open popover — it closes.
- Opening the filter popover while the sort popover is open should close the sort popover (and vice versa).

**Theme inheritance:**

- Switch the active theme to one with a dark background (or change the enclosing Group block's palette).
- All new UI (trigger borders, hover backgrounds, panel backgrounds, badge) should remain legible.

**Regression check:**

- Insert the original **Blog Search Page** pattern on another page. It should still render its full sidebar layout with the native `<select>` for sort and the same `search-results` "card" layout as before.

## Screenshots (from the issue, for reference)

Target initial UI, filter-open state, and filter-applied state are documented on [RSM-1071](https://linear.app/a8c/issue/RSM-1071/search-30-compact-search-pattern-with-inline-filter-sort-controls) — the one deliberate departure from Dataview is using a sort icon where Dataview uses a gear.

body:
## Summary
This PR fixes two issues in the Dashboard feature: ensuring stale projection data is cleared when loading fails, and correcting timezone handling in the cash flow chart calculations.

## Key Changes
- **DashboardView.swift**: 
  - Clear projections to `nil` when token is unavailable, ensuring the chart hides properly
  - Clear projections to `nil` on API errors instead of silently failing, preventing stale data from displaying
  
- **CashFlowChartView.swift**:
  - Use explicit UTC timezone for date calculations in `xDomain` to ensure consistent chart rendering across different device timezones
  - Replace implicit calendar with explicit Gregorian calendar configured with UTC timezone

## Implementation Details
The projection clearing ensures the UI responds correctly to both authentication and network failures by hiding the chart rather than displaying outdated information. The timezone fix prevents date calculation discrepancies that could occur when the device timezone differs from the expected UTC reference point for the chart's date range.

author: qcolombet
body:
The InlineSpiller tries to shorten the live-ranges used when storing a value that is defined by a sibling register by performing the following transformation:
```
a = copy b
store a
```
=>
```
store b
```
That is, it eliminates the copy and store the original value at the copy location.

As far as `b`'s live-range is concerned, this transformation is neutral as long as the store is inserted in place of the copy being removed.

That doesn't hold when the copy is part of the basic block prologue. In that case, the earliest insertion point for the store is after the prologue:
```
a = copy b # part of bb prologue
... # more prologue instrs
store a <-- earliest insertion point
```
Therefore when this optimization kicks in and the copy is in the bb's prologue, b's live-range needs to be extended to that insertion point.

This is exactly what this fix does.

Note: This issue is fairly easy to understand from an IR stand point and one would expect a small reproducer.
Indeed, we would need only something that looks like:
```
a = copy b # prologue compatible copy
# some more prologue instrs
# high pressure point
= use a
```

The problem is the InlineSpiller optimization (implemented in InlineSpiller::hoistSpillInsideBB) triggers only if `a` and `b` are sibling registers, meaning they are the product of a live-range splitting. Controlling live-range splitting is hard and I couldn't come up with a smaller test case. The problem also disappears if we run greedy alone because the live-ranges are repacked (well the slot indices to be exact) compared to what the scheduler produces. That changes the allocation order and the bug is not hit anymore.
The alternative would be to run the pipeline from the coalescer/scheduler but that's not a whole lot more robust than the LLVM IR path, plus the reproducer would be ~20k line long!

The other option (maybe something we should do in the long term) would be to serialize/deserialize the VirtRegMap object so that we can set the Virt2SplitMap map in a state that register a and b as siblings.

author: gnprice
body:
Fixes #1934.

This will cause the server to keep around the event queue for longer
periods of not hearing from the app: 12 hours, rather than 10 minutes.
That means if you open the app at several different times in the day,
it'll typically be immediately ready to go.


### Selected commit messages

c167cadf5 api [nfc]: Explain why registerQueue hard-codes many parameters



d09c0582c api [nfc]: Fill in registerQueue parameters we hard-code not passing

This doesn't cover parameters that were added in recent Zulip Server
versions; just those that in principle would have been mentioned
since early versions of this endpoint binding.

(The newer parameters will naturally be added separately when we
periodically sweep through the API changelog.)



7acb59c36 api: Add idleQueueTimeout parameter to registerQueue route

This is a bit overkill -- we'd have been fine just hard-coding to
the value "mobile".  But I figured I'd experiment with a new way
to express this sort of "int or enum" type.  This seems potentially
a bit cleaner, for the app code that consumes it, than the pattern
we have in places like Anchor (with AnchorCode and NumericAnchor).

(This bit of API is also a bit different from that one, in that
the "enum" values are in proper JSON.  But that's orthogonal to the
difference in the code-facing API here.)

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Two Resend call sites (`/api/auth/forgot-password` and `/form`) had `LibEdge ` hardcoded as the sender. That address only works once `libedge.com` is verified on Resend — until then every send fails with a 403 `domain is not verified` (silent in `/form`, since its errors are only logged). This PR makes the sender configurable: - New helper `getEmailFrom(c)` reads `c.env.EMAIL_FROM` and returns its trimmed value, falling back to the former literal if unset. - Both Resend fetch bodies now pass `getEmailFrom(c)` as `from`. - The password-reset email's plain-text footer now shows the configured sender's address rather than the hardcoded string, via a small regex that extracts the `` portion of the `EMAIL_FROM` value. No functional change when `EMAIL_FROM` is unset — the default matches prior behaviour. ### Usage after merge Point staging at the verified `selmiye.com` domain (once DNS verification is done on Resend): ```powershell npx wrangler secret put EMAIL_FROM --env staging # paste: LibEdge ``` Or, since the value isn't sensitive, put it under `[vars]` in `wrangler.toml` per env. I kept that out of this PR so we don't touch `wrangler.toml` when the domain choice is still provisional. author: leaharmstrong
body:
## Summary

Add optional `exact_prefix` and `exact_suffix` filters to the search functionality, enabling literal (non-regex) case-insensitive prefix/suffix matching on identifiers. These filters are ANDed with the regex query and provide a safer alternative to hand-escaping regex anchors for namespace and suffix scoping.

## Motivation

Users need a way to filter search results by identifier prefix or suffix without dealing with regex metacharacter escaping. For example, filtering by namespace like `"Next::Settings::"` requires escaping `::` in regex, which is error-prone. Literal prefix/suffix filters solve this by treating the filter value as plain text.

## Changes

- **lib/woods/mcp/index_reader.rb**
  - Add `exact_prefix` and `exact_suffix` optional parameters to `search()` method
  - Implement `identifier_passes_prefix_suffix?()` helper for case-insensitive literal matching
  - Implement `identifier_passes_filters?()` helper combining regex and prefix/suffix checks
  - Update broad-match detection to account for filtered candidate sets
  - Allow `query` parameter to be optional when prefix/suffix filters are provided
  - Raise `ArgumentError` when all of query, exact_prefix, and exact_suffix are blank
  - Add `require 'active_support/core_ext/object/blank'` for blank? checks

- **lib/woods/mcp/server.rb**
  - Update `define_search_tool()` to accept and pass through `exact_prefix` and `exact_suffix` parameters
  - Add `respond_err` parameter to `define_search_tool()` for structured error responses
  - Add validation that at least one of query/exact_prefix/exact_suffix is provided
  - Return structured error with helpful hint when all filters are missing
  - Update tool description and schema documentation

## Testing

- Added 18 comprehensive unit tests in `spec/mcp/index_reader_spec.rb` covering:
  - Basic prefix and suffix filtering
  - Case-insensitivity for both filters
  - Literal string handling (e.g., `::` metacharacters)
  - Combination with regex query (AND logic)
  - Combination of both prefix and suffix
  - Blank filter handling
  - Application to source_code field matches
  - Nil query acceptance with filters
  - ArgumentError validation
  - Composition with types and metadata filters
  - Broad-match warning behavior with filters

- Added 5 integration tests in `spec/mcp/server_spec.rb` covering:
  - Prefix filtering via tool call
  - Suffix filtering via tool call
  - Combination with regex query
  - Query-optional behavior
  - Structured error response when all filters missing

All existing tests continue to pass.

## Summary

Closes the three wiring gaps M7.9 flagged as follow-ups so the PM
supervisor primitives have runtime effect, not just storage effect:

- **Gap 1 — Agent drains `SupervisorInbox`**: `Agent::with_supervisor_inbox(rx)` + non-blocking drain call at the top of each loop turn in both `process_message_inner` and `run_task`. Drained messages are injected as synthetic user-role turns with a `[from: sender]` attribution prefix. Spawn wrapper transfers the receiver into the child worker.
- **Gap 2 — `relaunch_task` re-executes**: `TaskReexecutor` trait + `attach_reexecutor` on the supervisor. When attached, `relaunch_task` spawns a supervisor-owned tokio task that calls `SpawnTool::execute(merged_spec)` — the re-execution happens *not* on the parent agent's loop (which may have moved on). M7.9 plan-only path is preserved for raw callers.
- **Gap 3 — Matrix puppet steering consumer**: `SteeringInputConsumer` trait + `with_steering_consumer` builder + `handle_supervisor_reply` hook. Keeps `octos-bus` free of `octos-agent` deps (no cycle) while still letting Matrix supervisor replies route into the target child's inbox via `TaskSupervisor::send_to_agent`. New `octos_swarm_supervisor_steering_routed_total{outcome}` metric.

author: patrickdappollonio
body:
When dux detects that a repository isn't sitting on its default branch, the existing "Non-Default Branch" warning forces users out of the app to fix the state manually — `cd` into the repo, resolve any dirty tree, `git checkout main`, then come back and retry. For projects buried deep in the filesystem that round-trip is annoying enough to discourage adding projects in the first place.

This PR extends the warning modal with a **"Check out `<default_branch>` before adding"** checkbox (on by default) that appears whenever dux can confidently identify the default branch via `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`. Confirming with the box ticked runs `git checkout <default_branch>` in the source repo through a background worker — surfacing busy/success/error via the shared status API without blocking the UI thread — and only registers the project on success. Any commits on the previous branch stay put, untracked files and non-conflicting working-tree edits are preserved by git's normal checkout semantics, and conflicts produce an actionable status line with the full git error written to `dux.log` for post-mortem.

The heuristic path (no `origin/HEAD`, branch doesn't look like `main`/`master`) is deliberately unchanged: dux shows a dim *"can't confidently identify this repo's default branch, so it won't change branches for you"* note and keeps the original `Cancel` / `Add Anyway` buttons, because guessing at a target branch could land on something irrelevant or nonexistent. Focus cycles `Cancel → Add → Checkbox` via Tab (reverses with Shift-Tab) and the checkbox is independently clickable with the mouse, matching the Delete Agent modal pattern from #182. New unit tests cover `git::checkout_branch` across clean, missing-target, unrelated-dirty, and conflicting-dirty cases; `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and the full test suite pass.

author: rolandd
body:
💡 What: Replaced higher-order array methods (`.find()`, `.reduce()`) and `for...of` iterables with traditional indexed `for` loops in the `worker/src/gtfs-rt.ts` GTFS-RT parser. Also replaced eager array allocations with lazy array creation during service alert updates.

🎯 Why: The parsing functions sit on a very hot path handling large Protobuf arrays where every millisecond matters. Higher-order functions add significant closure and context object overhead. Iterators (like `for...of` loop over `Array`) also cause intermediate iterator instance allocations which can trigger the garbage collector more often. Removing these reduces parsing time.

📊 Impact: Running `tinybench` revealed substantial parser time reductions. For instance, parsing ServiceAlerts increased from ~163k ops/sec to ~168k ops/sec, and overall `buildRealtimeStatus` parsing time reduced from ~147k ns to ~142k ns on average.

🔬 Measurement: Verify the improvements by navigating to `cd worker` and running `pnpm run bench:gtfs-rt`.

author: diogo7dias
body:
This PR introduces the final Phase 3 optimizations for the custom font architecture, completing the PR #70 roadmap.

**Features Implemented:**
- **Shared Glyph Arena & Lazy Variant Loading:** Dramatically reduces heap consumption by only opening the font variants (e.g. bold, italic) when their glyphs are actually requested, utilizing a shared cache arena to prevent fragmentation.
- **Heap-Budget Scan Caps:** Added a strict 150 KB free heap check to `scanAndQueuePrompts()` to prevent system Out-of-Memory (OOM) resets when scanning massive font directories.
- **Zero-copy Scan-line Decode:** Optimized the core `decodeBitmap` loop. It no longer allocates a 192-byte stack buffer per line and avoids 1-byte virtual file reads, reading lines directly in optimal hex blocks for vastly improved page render times.
- **Async Install UX:** Transitioned the heavy `buildIndex()` execution into an asynchronous FreeRTOS task, preventing the main loop from locking up during Unifont installation.
- **Boot-loop Self-Recovery:** Added a safe-guard lock file. If the device panics while attempting to enumerate or register custom fonts, the next boot bypasses custom fonts, rescuing the device from permanent crash loops.

Please review the code changes and verify functionality. Ooga booga!

**Why:** `type='withdrawal'` has been declared in the ledger schema + shared types + openapi since day one but no production writer exists. With ADR 016's payout infrastructure live (pending_payouts queue, Stellar SDK submit, retry worker), the last missing piece is the ledger-side entry point.

**Decision highlights:**

- Admin-only for Phase 2a (`POST /api/admin/users/:userId/withdrawals`). User-initiated is Phase 2b.
- Atomic two-row write: pending_payouts row first (for id), then credit_transactions row referencing it, then balance decrement. All in one DB txn with FOR UPDATE on the balance row.
- Partial unique index extended to cover withdrawal/payout — at-most-one withdrawal row per payout id.
- Compensation on permanent payout failure via `type='adjustment'` (not refund — refund is order-scoped per migration 0013 §15). Admin-triggered for now.
- Response envelope parallels the refund handler.

**Implementation plan:** 4 follow-up PRs (ledger primitive + migration, handler + openapi, admin UI, compensation endpoint) documented in-file.

## Why now

Unblocks the last residual on A2-901 (the other two writers — refund and spend — are shipped, per PR #835). Also aligns with the /loop mandate: stablecoins for crediting users, admin treasury, the admin panel shape. Design-first keeps the implementation PRs reviewable in bite-size chunks.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/lint-docs.sh` passes
- [ ] After merge: confirm the ADR index in CLAUDE.md renders and ADR-024 is discoverable

body:
## Summary
- Adds `neo work finish [branch]` — completes the work trilogy. After a PR merges, it switches to the base branch, pulls, removes any associated worktree under `.worktrees/`, deletes the local branch, and marks the corresponding work-item in the agent context DB as done.
- Merge detection prefers `gh pr list --head <branch>` (the only reliable source for squash-merges) and falls back to `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> origin/<base>` when gh is unavailable or there's no PR. `--force` bypasses the merge check for abandoned branches.
- Refuses to delete the base branch, refuses to run with uncommitted changes on the current branch (unless `--force`), and refuses when merge status can't be confirmed. Worktree discovery uses `git worktree list --porcelain` so the path is authoritative rather than guessed from the branch name.

## Base

Stacked on [PR #21 (`neo work ship`)](https://github.com/radkode/neo/pull/21) → [PR #20 (`neo work start`)](https://github.com/radkode/neo/pull/20). Will retarget `main` after both merge.

## Test plan
- [ ] `neo work finish` on a merged branch switches to base, pulls, deletes the branch.
- [ ] `neo work finish <name>` on another branch works without switching to it first.
- [ ] `neo work finish --no-pull` skips the pull step.
- [ ] `neo work finish --keep-worktree` leaves the worktree in place.
- [ ] On base branch: errors with `Refusing to delete base branch "main"`.
- [ ] With uncommitted changes on current branch: errors unless `--force`.
- [ ] On an unmerged branch with no PR: errors with `Could not confirm ... is merged` unless `--force`.
- [ ] On an unmerged branch with an open PR (GH `state=OPEN`): errors with `PR for ... is not merged (<url>)` unless `--force`.
- [ ] With a worktree at `.worktrees/<name>`: the worktree directory and its metadata are removed.
- [ ] Agent context DB (if initialized): the `branch:<name>` work-item has `active` → `done` in tags and priority demoted to `low`.
- [ ] JSON mode round-trips through `jq` and emits `{ok:true, command:"work finish", ...}`.
- [ ] `neo schema | jq '.commands[] | select(.name == "work") | .commands[] | .name'` returns `start`, `ship`, `finish`.

author: samjmarshall
body:
## Context/Motivation

Two parallel workstreams that built on each other as the nurture feature was implemented:

1. **Nurture scheduler (ENG-132):** Without an automated scheduler, the message queue only fills when consultants manually trigger leads. This PR closes that gap by auto-starting stage-appropriate nurture sequences on lead create/update and running a Vercel Cron job daily to draft messages for due sequences.

2. **Claude harness improvements:** While working through ENG-132, several agent and tooling gaps surfaced (no dedicated web-research/lookup agents, git safety gaps in the heredoc-blocking script, missing E2E cleanup guardrails). These were fixed in the same branch.

## Description of Changes

### Nurture Scheduler (feat)

- **Scheduler** (`src/server/nurture/scheduler.ts`) — `runSchedulerTick` queries sequences where `nextStepAt <= now()`, drafts a message per sequence (sequential to amortise AI prompt-cache hits), inserts `pending` rows into `message_queue`, and advances `nextStepAt`. Errors log and advance anyway so a failing row never blocks the tick.
- **Auto-start wiring** (`leads.ts`) — `startOrUpdateSequence` called non-blockingly on `leadsRouter.create` and `.update`; failure logs but never blocks the lead operation. Cadence: `unqualified` → discovery/3d, `nurture` → nurture/14d, `warm` → warm_progression/7d. Hot leads auto-complete any active sequence.
- **tRPC router** (`nurture.ts`) — replaces the 7-line stub with `listActive`, `startSequence`, `pauseSequence`, `resumeSequence`.
- **Zod schemas** (`src/server/api/schemas/nurture.ts`) — typed input schemas for all mutations.
- **Cron route** (`GET /api/cron/nurture-scheduler`) — bearer-auth via `CRON_SECRET`, scheduled daily at 00:00 UTC in `vercel.json` (Hobby plan limit).
- **Dev helper** (`POST /api/dev/nurture/advance`) — backdates `nextStepAt` by 1 minute to trigger a tick without waiting; returns 404 in production.
- **AI stub** (`src/server/ai/stub.ts`) — deterministic draft function injected via `x-ai-stub: 1` header; enables E2E tests without calling the real AI.
- **DB migration** — partial unique index `nurture_active_one_per_lead_uidx ON (lead_id) WHERE status = 'active'` enforces one active sequence per lead at the DB level.
- **Env** — `CRON_SECRET` added to `src/env.js` (min 16 chars) and CI secrets.

### Claude Harness Improvements (chore)

- **New agents** — `web-lookup` (single-fact/library-docs, context7-first, 200-word cap) and `web-research` (deep multi-source synthesis, ≥3 sources, 800-word default cap, Opus model) replace the one-size-fits-all `web-search-researcher` for clearer routing.
- **`web-search-researcher`** — rewritten with hard contracts (citation, search budget, staleness, length budget), mandatory output format, and clear scope boundary vs the new agents.
- **`codebase-pattern-finder`** — upgraded from haiku to sonnet for better pattern extraction.
- **Git safety script** (`block-dangerous-git.sh`) — heredoc pattern detection improved; previously allowed dangerous commits when git args spanned multiple lines.
- **E2E cleanup skill** (`.claude/skills/tdd/e2e-cleanup.md`) — added as a TDD sub-file with per-spec cleanup, dotenv load order, flake double-run, and test data isolation rules.
- **CLAUDE.md** — added Vercel CLI section, Testing section, expanded E2E guardrails, and GitHub Actions note about dispatch triggers always running from `main`.
- **Makefile** — `vercel_link`, `env_pull`, `env_pull_preview` targets.
- **Command descriptors** — ultrathink prompts and routing hints tightened across `brainstorm`, `create_plan`, `describe_pr`, `implement_plan`, `iterate_plan`, `review_roadmap`, `validate_plan`, `write_ticket`.

## Testing Information

- [x] Unit tests pass (`make test`) — new suites: nurture schemas, scheduler, nurture router, cron route, leads auto-start, AI stub
- [x] `make check` passes (lint + typecheck)
- [ ] Integration tests pass (requires live Neon branch)
- [ ] Manual testing completed

**Test steps:**
1. `make check` — lint + typecheck
2. `make test` — unit tests (Rstest)
3. `make test_e2e` — Playwright E2E (`e2e/features/nurture-scheduler.spec.ts` covers auto-start, cron tick, pause/resume, hot-lead completion)
4. Manual: seed a lead, call `POST /api/dev/nurture/advance`, hit `GET /api/cron/nurture-scheduler` with the `CRON_SECRET` bearer token, confirm a `pending` row appears in `message_queue`

## Screenshots/Videos

N/A — no UI changes.

## Relevant Links

- Closes #132

## Breaking Changes

**BREAKING CHANGE:** `CRON_SECRET` env var is now required (minimum 16 characters). Vercel sets this automatically for cron routes; local `.env.local` must be re-pulled via `make env_pull` after this merges.

### Motivation
- Reduce hover latency during idle while avoiding CPU spikes during active interaction by replacing a single fixed hit-test interval with an adaptive policy.
- Make hover behavior more responsive to micro-movements when idle while keeping conservative cadence during drags/interactions.
- Add lightweight telemetry so we can validate queries/sec and average resolution time without shipping expensive instrumentation.

### Description
- Replaced the fixed `kHoverHitTestIntervalMs` with two constants: `kHoverHitTestIdleIntervalMs = 10` and `kHoverHitTestInteractingIntervalMs = 35` and added `kHoverIdleMoveThresholdPx = 0` in `viewer2d/viewer2dpanel.h`.
- Added `GetHoverHitTestIntervalMs()` and `GetHoverMoveThresholdPx()` helpers and updated `ScheduleHoverHitTest(...)` to pick interval/threshold based on `m_dragMode`, `m_isInteracting` and recent view motion (`m_viewMotionSinceLastHoverHitTest`).
- Kept `kHoverMoveThresholdPx` for drag state while effectively disabling the idle movement threshold to allow faster responses to micro-movements; set `m_viewMotionSinceLastHoverHitTest` on view change, pan drag and mouse-wheel zoom to keep the interacting cadence while motion is recent.
- Added debug-only telemetry (`TrackHoverHitTestTelemetry`) that accumulates hover queries per second and average resolution time (ms) and logs them via `wxLogDebug` to validate latency vs CPU trade-offs; telemetry fields and windowing added to the panel state.

### Testing
- Ran `tests/check_perastage_tree_modules.sh` and it passed (OK).
- Ran `tests/check_no_configmanager_get_in_gui.sh` and it passed (OK).
- Manual build/compile was exercised implicitly by running the checks and no module-boundary changes were introduced; telemetry is gated under `#ifndef NDEBUG` so it only logs in debug builds.

author: twigotter
body:
## Summary
This PR adds hand pose detection and animation to the VRM model using MediaPipe's HandLandmarker. Hands are now tracked from the webcam feed and finger bones are animated in real-time based on detected hand landmarks.

## Key Changes
- **Hand Landmark Detection**: Imported `HandLandmarker` from MediaPipe and created `loadHandLandmarker()` function to initialize hand detection with GPU acceleration, supporting up to 2 hands in video mode
- **Hand Bone Mapping**: Added comprehensive bone mappings for both left and right hands, covering wrist and all finger joints (thumb, index, middle, ring, little fingers with their metacarpal/proximal/intermediate/distal segments)
- **Hand Pose Application**: Implemented `applyHandPose()` function that:
  - Calculates wrist rotation using 3-DOF (pitch, yaw, roll) based on finger direction and palm normal
  - Applies finger chain kinematics to animate individual finger bones
  - Properly transforms hand landmarks from world space to local bone space
- **Filtering**: Added One-Euro filters for hand landmarks (21 landmarks × 3 axes × 2 hands) to smooth noisy detection data
- **Hand Detection Loop**: Integrated hand detection into the main animation loop with:
  - Per-frame hand landmark detection and filtering
  - Automatic hand side detection (left/right) from MediaPipe confidence scores
  - Reset of hand bones when hands are not detected to prevent frozen poses

## Implementation Details
- Hand landmark indices are organized in a `HLM` constant for clarity (wrist at index 0, fingers at indices 1-20)
- Wrist rotation uses a two-step quaternion approach: first aligning finger direction (pitch+yaw), then aligning palm normal (roll)
- Finger chains are processed sequentially, with each bone's rotation computed relative to its parent's world quaternion
- Hand pose is anchored to the lower arm's world quaternion for proper integration with existing arm tracking

## Summary

Implements the dry-run shell of the ADR-0018 ICP agent runtime (GitHub Actions + Claude Code Action). This ticket is scoped to the workflow harness only — no Anthropic calls, no Claude Code Action invocation, no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` requirement. Live provider wiring is owned by LAT-69 (secret + workflow configuration) and LAT-67 (first end-to-end dispatch).

- New workflow `.github/workflows/icp-runtime-harness.yml`, triggered by `workflow_dispatch` with inputs: `ticket` (LAT-<digits>), `skill`, `dry_run` (boolean, default true), `cost_band` (optional).
- `dry_run=true` job: checks out, sets up Node from `.nvmrc`, runs `npm ci`, runs `npm run check`, and emits a sanitized `artifacts/icp-runtime-dry-run.md` summary plus a `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` entry. The summary contains only operator-supplied inputs and the guardrail pass signal — no provider output, no secrets.
- `dry_run=false` job: refuses explicitly with a pointer to LAT-69 / LAT-67 and exits non-zero.
- Least-privilege posture per ADR-0018: `permissions: contents: read`, no `actions: write`, no secrets referenced, no custom `github_token`, no `allowed_bots` / `allowed_non_write_users`, no fork-PR triggers.
- Operator-facing comment block at the top of the workflow makes the dry-run-only scope obvious and flags the ADR-0008 "agents do not edit CI" rule.

## Testing

- [x] `npm ci` (clean install on Node 20).
- [x] `npm run check` passes locally (typecheck, build, validate:adrs, validate:prds, policy-scan, tests).
- [x] `node packages/secret-guard/dist/cli.js .github/workflows/icp-runtime-harness.yml` — no findings.
- [x] `node packages/secret-guard/dist/cli.js --staged` — no findings.
- [x] YAML syntactic validity verified with `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(...))"`. Workflow semantics (GitHub-specific `on`, `permissions`, `jobs.*.if`, expressions) could not be exercised without a live dispatch; they follow the ADR-0018 shape and standard GitHub Actions conventions used by the existing `check.yml`.
- [ ] Not executed: live `workflow_dispatch` run. Intentionally deferred — the runtime shell proves out the first time an operator dispatches it from the GitHub UI post-merge. Dry-run semantics are the point of this PR.

## Scope notes

- Does not edit any shared Markdown hub / index.
- Does not add or modify ADRs — ADR-0018 already names the constraints this harness satisfies.
- Does not introduce comment/label triggers, branch protection changes, or any provider secret.

body:
## Summary

- Threads a new `entry_direction: \"debit\" | \"credit\"` field (from the `DCStrategySpec` API payload) through `LegData` into `LegDetailBlock`.
- `NetDebitHeader` colors the post-entry delta by \"in our favor\" — debit rising after entry = profit = green; credit falling after entry = decay = green. Label becomes \"Net Credit\" for credit-direction strategies. Pre-entry coloring still follows \"rising = pay more\" for the cost-to-enter view.
- `ProfitTargetLine` computes `basis × (1 − pct)` for credit structures (e.g. $3.00 straddle with 25% TP → $2.25 target, labeled \"TP 25% decay\") and keeps the existing `basis × (1 + pct)` for debit.

## Why

Two trader-flagged usability bugs:

Paired with backend PR #71 on vega-pilot, which adds `entry_direction` to the spec schema. Until both merge + the API redeploys, this code falls back to `\"debit\"` behavior for every strategy (backend default).

body:
## What's in here

A mechanical cleanup pass on the way to a design-only tool. No UI rework yet, no behavior changes for design mode. Everything typechecks, lints, and formats. ~25k net lines deleted across six commits.

### 1. `chore: delete apps/desktop, apps/marketing, and all release tooling`

Electron wrapper, standalone marketing site, and the entire desktop release pipeline (multi-platform signed builds, auto-updater, nightly channel, release smoke). Design-harness is a web tool; none of this applies.

- Delete `apps/desktop/` (31 files) and `apps/marketing/` entirely.
- Delete desktop-only scripts: `build-desktop-artifact`, `release-smoke`, `merge-update-manifests`, `mock-update-server`, `resolve-nightly-release`, `resolve-previous-release-tag`, `update-release-package-versions`, `scripts/lib/build-target-arch`, `scripts/lib/update-manifest`.
- Drop marketing/desktop npm scripts (`dev:marketing`, `dev:desktop`, `dist:desktop:*`, `release:smoke`, `test:desktop-smoke`), the `T3CODE_DESKTOP_WS_URL` env var, and `dist-electron/**` build output from turbo.json.
- Delete `.github/workflows/release.yml`, trim desktop steps from `ci.yml`.
- Simplify `scripts/dev-runner` — drop the `dev:desktop` mode and all related env-var plumbing.
- Drop stale docs: `docs/release.md`, `.docs/ci.md`, `.docs/scripts.md`, desktop snippets from `docs/observability.md`.

The dead `window.desktopBridge` fallback paths in web (`env.isElectron`, `branding`, `localApi`, etc.) are kept as-is for now — they're already graceful fallbacks that just never fire without a bridge. Easy cleanup for a follow-up.

### 2. `chore: rip ProjectSetupScriptRunner + UI + runSetupScript wiring`

Design threads never invoke project setup scripts. Drops the server runner, the entire UI, the web-side helpers, and the `runSetupScript` flag that used to ride along on thread turn start.

- Delete `apps/server/src/project/{Services,Layers}/ProjectSetupScriptRunner.ts` + tests.
- Delete `apps/web/src/projectScripts.{ts,test}`, `apps/web/src/lib/projectScriptKeybindings.{ts,test}`, `apps/web/src/components/ProjectScriptsControl.tsx`.
- Delete `packages/shared/src/projectScripts.ts` + its workspace export.
- Unwire the runner from `server.ts`, `ws.ts`, `GitManager.ts`, and the matching test scaffolding.
- Drop `runSetupScript` from `ThreadTurnStartBootstrap` in contracts + `ChatView.tsx` + `ChatView.browser.tsx` + orchestration test.
- Drop the `runProjectScript` helper + keybinding dispatch + `LAST_INVOKED_SCRIPT_BY_PROJECT_KEY` from `ChatView.tsx`; inline the trivial `projectScriptCwd` helper.

The `scripts` field on `OrchestrationProject` stays in place — a future migration can drop the column cleanly once nothing touches it.

### 3. `chore: unwire git write RPCs + GitActionsControl UI from web`

The tool never mutates git state — it writes HTML to `.t3code/design`. Drops the RPC surface + web UI + worktree bootstrap path. Read-only status RPCs (`pull`, `refreshStatus`, `listBranches`, `subscribeGitStatus`) stay.

- `ws.ts`: delete 8 RPC handlers (`gitRunStackedAction`, `gitResolvePullRequest`, `gitPreparePullRequestThread`, `gitCreateWorktree`, `gitRemoveWorktree`, `gitCreateBranch`, `gitCheckout`, `gitInit`) and the `prepareWorktree` branch of `thread.turn.start` bootstrap.
- `contracts/rpc.ts` + `ipc.ts`: drop the 8 `Rpc` definitions, method names, `EnvironmentApi.git` methods, and `WsRpcGroup` members.
- Web: delete `GitActionsControl{.tsx,.browser.tsx,.logic.ts,.logic.test.ts}`, drop the write mutations from `gitReactQuery` (now only `pull` + infinite branch search), delete `gitReactQuery.test.ts`.
- `ChatView.tsx`: drop the worktree bootstrap flow (`buildTemporaryWorktreeBranchName`, `baseBranchForWorktree`, `prepareWorktree`); drop the associated browser tests.
- `useThreadActions.ts`: drop orphaned-worktree removal on thread delete.
- Tests: delete the `"routes websocket rpc git methods"` block, the three `gitRunStackedAction` test blocks in `server.test.ts`, and references in `wsTransport.test.ts` / `wsRpcHarness.ts`.

**Kept deliberately for now:** `GitManager` and `GitCore` Effect layers still contain the underlying write helpers (`resolvePullRequest`, `preparePullRequestThread`, `runStackedAction`, `createWorktree`, etc.). They're unreachable from the outside after this PR, but the surrounding `GitManager.test.ts` / `GitCore.test.ts` / `CheckpointStore.test.ts` / integration tests still exercise them, and ripping them out would balloon this PR.

### 4. `chore: apply oxfmt to the files touched by the cleanup`

Purely cosmetic.

### 5. `chore: rip the terminal module end-to-end`

Design threads never open a shell. Drops the PTY layer, the 7 terminal RPCs, the whole web terminal state machine, and the dead CI config.

- **Server**: delete `apps/server/src/terminal/` (Manager service + layer, BunPTY/NodePTY adapters, tests). Drop `TerminalManagerLive` + `PtyAdapterLive` from `server.ts`, the `TerminalManager` yield + 7 RPC handlers + `subscribeTerminalEvents` from `ws.ts`, the `terminalManager.close` cleanup from `ThreadDeletionReactor` and `ws.ts` archive flow, `terminalManager` usage from `server.test.ts`. Drop `terminalSessionsTotal` / `terminalRestartsTotal` metrics and `terminalLogsDir` config. Delete the three terminal-archive server tests and the terminal RPC test block.
- **Contracts**: delete `packages/contracts/src/terminal.ts` + tests, drop the re-export from the index barrel. Strip the terminal RPC entries, methods, and schemas from `rpc.ts`; drop `EnvironmentApi.terminal` from `ipc.ts`.
- **Web**: delete `terminalStateStore{,.test}`, `terminalActivity{,.test}`. Drop `EnvironmentApi.terminal` routing from `environmentApi.ts`, the terminal interface from `rpc/wsRpcClient.ts`. Rip the terminal event pipeline from `environments/runtime` (connection + service), plus the dead `shouldApplyTerminalEvent` helper + its test file. Strip terminal state/UI/keybindings from `ChatView.tsx` (state subscriptions, open/split/new/close callbacks, launch-context effects, four terminal keybindings); drop `api.terminal.close` on thread delete in `useThreadActions`; drop terminal-running indicators from `Sidebar` + `ThreadStatusIndicators` + `ThreadRowTrailingStatus`; drop `terminalOpen` context threading through `_chat` route + `CommandPalette`. Delete terminal-dependent tests + setState blocks from `ChatView.browser.tsx` and `localApi.test.ts`; drop `subscribeTerminalEvents` from `wsRpcHarness`.

`terminal-links.{ts,test.ts}` stays — it's path-link parsing used by markdown/file-path rendering, not terminal state. `isTerminalFocused` and the `"Terminal process running"` status label constants also stay (harmless now, stylistic followup).

### 6. `chore(composer): remove /plan + /default slash commands`

Users can't enter plan mode from the UI now that the tool is design-only; the `/default` entry only existed as its twin. The `ComposerPlanFollowUpBanner` UI and `proposedPlans` data flow remain — they're server-driven and will simply never trigger without plan mode being selected. A deeper sweep of `proposedPlan` threading (UI banner, server projection, timeline rendering) is a followup.

## Still pending (follow-up PRs)

- **GitManager/GitCore internal write helpers** — unreachable from the RPC surface, but still live in the Effect layers and referenced by a big chunk of `GitManager.test.ts` / `GitCore.test.ts` / `CheckpointStore.test.ts` / integration tests. Ripping them means deleting + rewriting hundreds of test cases.
- **Project `scripts` column** on `OrchestrationProject` (schema + projector + decider + migration + web store).
- **`proposedPlans` deep cleanup** — server-side projection, timeline rendering, `ComposerPlanFollowUpBanner`, `activeProposedPlan` in ChatView, `hasActionableProposedPlan` selectors.
- **Dead `desktopBridge` fallback paths** in web + `isElectron` branches.
- **Plan mode in `ProviderInteractionMode`** (the type still has `"plan"`; Codex adapter still has `PLAN_MODE_DEVE

author: theioz
body:
## Summary
- Closes #455. Adds an `async headers()` block to `web/next.config.ts` serving five security response headers on every route: `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy` (camera/mic/geolocation/interest-cohort denied), and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- CSP ships in **Report-Only** mode during a 7-day soak — directive gaps surface as browser-console warnings without breaking production. A follow-up one-line PR will flip `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` to `Content-Security-Policy` after the soak.
- New Playwright spec `web/smoke/specs/security-headers.spec.ts` asserts all five headers on `/login` (unauthenticated) and `/dashboard` (authenticated). The existing `chat.spec.ts` `consoleErrors.toHaveLength(0)` assertion doubles as the CSP-violation regression net — any `Refused to …` browser error during a live chat turn fails the test.

## CSP directive list
```
default-src 'self';
script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
img-src 'self' data: https://a.espncdn.com https://*.supabase.co;
font-src 'self' data:;
connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co wss://*.supabase.co;
frame-ancestors 'none';
base-uri 'self';
form-action 'self';
object-src 'none';
upgrade-insecure-requests
```

Notes on scoping:
- `connect-src` only lists Supabase — Anthropic, Polygon, ESPN API, ntfy, and googleapis are server-side only and don't belong in a browser CSP.
- `img-src` and `connect-src` pre-allow `https://*.supabase.co` / `wss://*.supabase.co` for forthcoming Supabase Storage (meal photos) and Realtime subscriptions, to avoid a CSP-update PR when those ship.
- `'unsafe-inline'` on `script-src` and `style-src` is required for Next 16 + React 19 hydration and Radix portals. A separate follow-up issue will harden with nonces via middleware.

## Local verification
`curl -sI http://localhost:3000/login` after `npm run dev`:
```
Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; …
X-Frame-Options: DENY
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), interest-cohort=()
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
```
All five headers also verified on `/api/chat`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Vercel preview deploy green
- [ ] CI green (tsc, token-lint, lint)
- [ ] `npm run smoke:chat` — chat turn completes with zero console errors (CSP regression net)
- [ ] New `smoke/specs/security-headers.spec.ts` passes
- [ ] `curl -I <preview-url>/` shows all five headers
- [ ] Post-merge: `curl -I https://mr-bridge-assistant.vercel.app/` on production confirms headers applied
- [ ] Soak week: spot-check devtools Console on /chat, /dashboard, /fitness, /recipes, /calendar, /habits, /settings for Report-Only violations
- [ ] Follow-up PR opened to flip CSP from Report-Only to enforcing
- [ ] Follow-up issue opened to drop `'unsafe-inline'` via nonce injection (Option E)

### Notable Features

* breaking change: need to update keybindings
* much more configurable with ~/.config/kitty-meow/meow.toml
* notable new features
  * project aliases & project sets 
  * gh cli auth support
  * global and project based templates

## Wall of Text

### Breaking changes from the Python version

 - Single binary replaces all kittens. Install kitty-meow and update your keybindings.
 - Config file required. Run kitty-meow init to generate one interactively, or create ~/.config/kitty-meow/meow.toml manually.
 - Config dir moved from ~/.config/kitty/meow/ to ~/.config/kitty-meow/.
 - Flags removed. --dir, --user, --org, BIN_PATH are all replaced by meow.toml.
 - See the migration guide (README.md#migrating-from-the-python-version) for a full before/after.

### New features

 - Project sets — open multiple related projects at once with a single selection
 - Project aliases — short tab titles with per-project pane templates
 - History — recently visited projects surfaced in the picker
 - Close tabs from the picker — built-in fzf keybinding, no separate kill.py needed
 - Configurable fzf keybindings — all source-switch bindings are configurable in meow.toml
 - kitty-meow init — interactive setup wizard that fetches your GitHub orgs and generates a config
 - kitty-meow version — prints version, commit, and build date
 - kitty-meow cache — list, refresh, and remove caches; auto-caches on first remote fetch
 - GitHub auth via gh CLI — no need to set GITHUB_TOKEN if you use the gh CLI
 - WezTerm support (experimental)
 - Goreleaser CI — pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, Windows on every tag

### Fixes

 - Cache miss no longer silently skips writing the cache — repos are now persisted on first fetch
 - Cache write errors no longer surface as fetch failures (valid repos are returned regardless)
 - 15-second HTTP timeout on all GitHub API calls
 - fzf reload commands now shell-quote the executable path (handles spaces in install paths)
 - GraphQL response unmarshal errors are now surfaced rather than silently returning zero repos

# Unify Mobile Tab Bars into a Shared `MobileTabBar` Molecule

## 🎯 Summary

Three structurally identical mobile tab-bar components (`ProfilePageMobileMenu`, `SettingsMobileMenu`, and the newly added `HotMobileMenu`) existed because this repeated pattern was not initially made into a reusable component. This PR extracts a single shared **`MobileTabBar`** molecule that owns the visual + a11y contract, and migrates all three call sites onto it.

Delivered as a **follow-up PR targeting the original `HotMobileMenu` PR branch** so reviewers can evaluate the unification in isolation from the Hot-page feature work.

## 🧱 What changed

### New shared component
- `src/components/molecules/MobileTabBar/MobileTabBar.tsx`
- `src/components/molecules/MobileTabBar/MobileTabBar.types.ts`
- `src/components/molecules/MobileTabBar/MobileTabBar.test.tsx` (+ snapshot)
- `src/components/molecules/MobileTabBar/index.ts`
- Registered in `src/components/molecules/index.ts`

**API highlights:**
- Per-item `isActive` + `onSelect` (not a global `activeKey`) — keeps `requireAuth` wrapping, `pathname` comparisons, and `setState` setters natural in consumers.
- `showLabels` toggles icon-only vs icon + label.
- `position` toggles between `sticky top-(--header-height-mobile)` and `fixed top-(--header-height-mobile) right-0 left-0`.
- `className` is merged last via `cn(...)` so consumers can append margin overrides without fighting defaults.
- `data-testid` passthrough + `aria-label` default (with optional override) + `aria-current="page"` on active.

### Migrated consumers (thin adapters)
- **`HotMobileMenu`** → `<MobileTabBar showLabels position="sticky" className="-mx-6 -mt-6 mb-6" ... />`. Keeps `HOT_MOBILE_MENU_ITEMS`, `HotSection`, and `hot.*` i18n.
- **`ProfilePageMobileMenu`** → `<MobileTabBar position="sticky" ... />`. Preserves `PROFILE_MENU_ITEMS` export, `isOwnProfile` filtering, `requireAuth`-wrapped clicks, and raw English labels.
- **`SettingsMobileMenu`** → `<MobileTabBar position="fixed" ... />`. Keeps `useTranslations('settings.menu')`, `SETTINGS_MOBILE_ITEMS`, and `usePathname`/`useRouter` selection.

## ⚠️ Behavioral change (intentional, scoped)

**Settings z-index consolidation:** `z-(--z-sticky-header)` (20) → `z-(--z-mobile-menu)` (30), which is the variable documented for mobile navigation and the value already used by Profile + Hot. This was a silent drift that this refactor corrects.

No other behavior changes:
- Settings remains `fixed`; Profile + Hot remain `sticky`.
- Hot keeps its `-mx-6 -mt-6 mb-6` layout overrides via `className` passthrough.
- Profile `requireAuth` and `isOwnProfile` filtering are preserved.
- i18n namespaces are unchanged.
- `lg:hidden` still hides all three on desktop.

## 🧹 Drive-by fix

Removed a stale literal string (`'data-testid="profile-page-mobile-menu-item"'`) that was being passed into `cn(...)` as a className in the old `ProfilePageMobileMenu` render block. It had no effect but was technically invalid class input.

## 🧪 Tests

- **`MobileTabBar`** — 18 tests: item rendering, icon-only vs `showLabels`, sticky + fixed positioning, always-applied root classes, active vs inactive states (border, icon color, `aria-current`), click dispatch, `aria-label` default + override, `className` merge, `data-testid` passthrough, button class toggling.
- **`HotMobileMenu`** — 9 tests, trimmed to behavior-level assertions (label rendering, `-mx-6 -mt-6 mb-6` passthrough, sticky, `data-testid`, `aria-current`, click wiring). Snapshot regenerated.
- **`ProfilePageMobileMenu`** — 8 tests. Added explicit coverage for `isOwnProfile={false}` filtering and `requireAuth`-gated click dispatch via `vi.mock('@/hooks', ...)`. Snapshot regenerated.
- **`SettingsMobileMenu`** — 5 tests. Added explicit `z-(--z-mobile-menu)` assertion + negative assertion against the old `z-(--z-sticky-header)`, plus a `fixed` positioning assertion. Snapshot regenerated.
- **Consumer suites** — `templates/Feed/Hot` (17) and `templates/Settings` (40) all pass with zero prop changes.

**Totals:** 97 targeted tests ✅ · `yarn tsc --noEmit` ✅ · `yarn lint` ✅

## 📦 File inventory

**New**
- `src/components/molecules/MobileTabBar/MobileTabBar.tsx`
- `src/components/molecules/MobileTabBar/MobileTabBar.types.ts`
- `src/components/molecules/MobileTabBar/MobileTabBar.test.tsx`
- `src/components/molecules/MobileTabBar/MobileTabBar.test.tsx.snap`
- `src/components/molecules/MobileTabBar/index.ts`

**Modified**
- `src/components/molecules/index.ts`
- `src/components/molecules/HotMobileMenu/HotMobileMenu.tsx`
- `src/components/molecules/HotMobileMenu/HotMobileMenu.test.tsx`
- `src/components/molecules/HotMobileMenu/HotMobileMenu.test.tsx.snap`
- `src/components/molecules/ProfilePageMobileMenu/ProfilePageMobileMenu.tsx`
- `src/components/molecules/ProfilePageMobileMenu/ProfilePageMobileMenu.test.tsx`
- `src/components/molecules/ProfilePageMobileMenu/ProfilePageMobileMenu.test.tsx.snap`
- `src/components/molecules/Settings/SettingsMobileMenu/SettingsMobileMenu.tsx`
- `src/components/molecules/Settings/SettingsMobileMenu/SettingsMobileMenu.test.tsx`
- `src/components/molecules/Settings/SettingsMobileMenu/SettingsMobileMenu.test.tsx.snap`

## 🚧 Deferred / follow-ups

- **Phase 5 (optional):** investigate whether Settings can move from `fixed` to `sticky` (would eliminate the last positioning fork). Deferred to keep this PR's behavior change surface minimal.
- **Future i18n sweep:** `PROFILE_MENU_ITEMS` still uses raw English labels while Hot and Settings use translation keys. Out of scope here.

## Related

This PR was created to directly address this review comment https://github.com/pubky/pubky-app/pull/1632#pullrequestreview-4075361705.

When `allowExceptInFunctions` (or `allowExceptInMethods` / `disallowInFunctions` / `disallowInMethods`) contained more than one entry, only calls from functions **not** matching the very first entry were correctly disallowed. Any call from a function matching the first entry would pass through to the second entry, which wouldn't match, causing an early `return true` (allowed).

**Root cause:** the loop bailed out on the first non-match instead of continuing:

```php
// Before — returns allowed on first non-match, never checks remaining entries
foreach ($disallowed->getAllowExceptInCalls() as $call) {
    if (!$this->callMatches($scope, $call)) {
        return true;
    }
}
```

**Fix:** restructured to match the identical pattern already used by `getAllowExceptIn()` (path-based checks):

```php
// After — returns forbidden on any match; allowed only after all entries pass
if ($disallowed->getAllowExceptInCalls()) {
    foreach ($disallowed->getAllowExceptInCalls() as $call) {
        if ($this->callMatches($scope, $call)) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}
```

- **`src/Allowed/Allowed.php`** — restores the correct guard + loop logic
- **`tests/Calls/FunctionCallsAllowExceptInMultipleMethodsTest.php`** — new test asserting that both entries in a two-element `allowExceptInMethods` list are enforced
- **`tests/src/RoyaleMultiple.php`** — fixture: three methods calling `crc32()`, two in the except list (expect errors), one outside (expect silence)

## Summary

MCP `apply_update` ツールに **Golden Gate** を追加し、golden test 未 pass の候補 YAML が誤って適用されるのを **API レベルで防止** する。

- **Option C ハイブリッド**: `last_golden_result` が渡されれば再利用し、未指定なら `_tool_run_golden_tests` を内部実行する（Cache 最適化 + Default Safe）
- **デフォルト ON**: `golden_pass_required=True` がデフォルト。明示的に `False` を渡すと旧挙動（ゲートなし）
- **Silent Success 防止**: golden case 未定義時は `warnings: ["no_golden_cases_defined"]` を返して apply 許可（エージェントへ明示通知）
- **構造化エラー**: 未 pass 時は `{error: "golden_not_passed", summary: {total, passed, failed}, hint: ...}` を返し、`save_workflow_with_backup` を呼ばない（書込スキップ）

author: faisyrs
body:
## Summary

A batch of related fixes that surfaced while chasing a single `elspais checks`-vs-`elspais fix` disagreement. CI on this PR revealed a further latent bug in fix itself, which is addressed by the third commit.

### Commits

1. **`40570b3` — checks/fix alignment, INDEX.md idempotence, `_classify_node` CWD fix**
   - `check_spec_changelog_present` now activates when either `changelog.present` OR `changelog.hash_current` is set, matching fix's gating. Previously fix would add changelog entries that checks had reported as fine.
   - Extracted `_build_index_content` so `_fix_index` and `check_spec_index_current` byte-compare against the same rendered content. `fix --dry-run` no longer prints "Would regenerate INDEX.md" when the file is already current, and the staleness check now catches title/order/format drift, not just missing IDs.
   - `_classify_node` uses FILE-node `absolute_path` instead of re-resolving repo-relative paths against CWD. Classification now works for library / MCP / federation callers that haven't chdir'd to the project.

2. **`18256ae` — `ELSPAIS_VERSION` env reservation**
   - `ELSPAIS_VERSION` is a min-CLI-version gate consumed by `utilities/version_check.py`, not a config override. The generic `ELSPAIS_*` → config-key sweep was mapping it onto the top-level `version` schema field (int), so downstream pre-commit hooks exporting `ELSPAIS_VERSION=0.x.y` produced a misleading "invalid literal for int() with base 10" error attributed to `.elspais.toml`. Added `_RESERVED_ENV_VARS = {"ELSPAIS_VERSION"}` and skip those in the override loop.

3. **`3c5ae5e` — `_fix_parse_dirty` actually persists missing Changelog sections**
   - Latent bug exposed by commit 1: `_fix_parse_dirty` excluded `missing_changelog`-only nodes from the autofix path, AND `_add_autofix_changelog_entries` read reasons from `parse_dirty_reasons` (set by the parser at build time and never containing `missing_changelog`, which only `_detect_fixable` discovers). Net effect: fix printed "Fixing REQ-X: add missing changelog section" and "Rewrote <file>" but wrote byte-identical content because no code path ever added the entry to the graph.
   - Refactored `_add_autofix_changelog_entries` to take explicit `(node, reasons)` tuples, routed all non-drift-only fixable nodes through it, and reordered so `mark_parse_dirty` runs before the autofix call.
   - Includes the 11 spec files + INDEX.md that `elspais fix` now correctly writes — the one-time baseline of changelog entries for elspais's own requirements under the newly-enforced check.

## Tests

- `tests/commands/test_checks_fix_consistency.py` — acceptance guard: on a clean fixture `run_spec_checks` passes, `_fix_index(dry_run=True)` emits no "Would" lines, `_detect_fixable` is empty for every REQUIREMENT, and classification works from an unrelated CWD.
- `tests/test_config_env_overrides.py` — reserved-var carve-out and confirmation that non-reserved overrides still apply.
- `tests/commands/test_fix_changelog.py::test_REQ_p00004_A_batch_fix_persists_missing_changelog` — regression guard for the batch-fix persistence bug.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit + integration suite: 3570 passed
- [x] Reproduced original `ELSPAIS_VERSION=0.112.13 elspais fix --dry-run` scenario in an unrelated project → now clean; previously died with the misleading int-parse error
- [x] Verified `elspais checks --spec` passes (HEALTHY: 15/15) against the elspais repo itself after the fix
- [x] Pre-commit hook (ruff + black + `elspais fix` + full test suite) clean on all three commits
- [x] CI green on this PR including Self-Validate Specs (previously failed before the third commit)

body:
## Summary
Fixes two bugs from `bugs.txt`:
- **Can't unlike** — tapping the heart a second time did nothing; the lambda only incremented.
- **Likes "affect all cards"** — each `SwipeCard` owned its own `useState(card.likeCount)`, which reset on remount when keys shifted between swipe slots and was not shared across multiple videos of the same restaurant.

## Changes
- **`frontend/src/components/SwipeCard.jsx`** — made controlled. It now receives `liked`, `likeCount`, and `onToggleLike` from the parent and no longer owns like state.
- **`frontend/src/pages/Feed.jsx`** — lifts like state into `Feed`, keyed by `placeId`. Displayed count = `card.likeCount + delta[placeId]`. Toggle fires `POST /like?placeId=...&action=like|unlike`.
- **`lambda/lambda.py`** — `/like` now accepts `action=unlike` and decrements `likeCount` with a `ConditionExpression` so it cannot go below zero (swallows `ConditionalCheckFailedException`). Also switches the increment to `if_not_exists(likeCount, 0) + 1` so missing attributes don't blow up.

## Test plan
- [ ] Tap heart on a card — count increments and heart turns red.
- [ ] Tap again — count decrements back and heart turns white.
- [ ] Swipe to another card — its count shows its own `likeCount` (plus any locally-tracked delta), not the previous card's bumped value.
- [ ] Swipe back to a previously-liked card — heart and count are still the liked state.
- [ ] If a restaurant has multiple videos, liking on one reflects on the others (they share `placeId`).
- [ ] Backend: DynamoDB `likeCount` does not go negative when repeatedly unliking.
